name: Marie Curie
bio: Marie Skłodowska Curie was a pioneer in radioactivity research and the first person awarded two Nobel Prizes.
contribution: Discovered radioactivity, isolated polonium and radium, and developed techniques for measuring radioactivity.

name: Albert Einstein
bio: Theoretical physicist who developed the theories of special and general relativity.
contribution: Theory of relativity, mass-energy equivalence (E=mc^2), contributions to quantum theory.

name: C. V. Raman
bio: Indian physicist known for the Raman effect in light scattering.
contribution: Discovery of the Raman effect, which provided insight into light-matter interactions.

name: Emmy Noether
bio: Mathematician whose theorem established the connection between symmetries and conservation laws in physics.
contribution: Noether's theorem linking symmetries and conservation laws, foundational for modern theoretical physics.

name: Léon Foucault
bio: French physicist and astronomer whose precision experiments made the motion of Earth visible.
contribution: His Foucault pendulum demonstrated Earth's rotation, and the Foucault knife-edge test measured the quality of telescope mirrors.

name: James Dewar
bio: Scottish physicist and chemist known for pioneering work in low-temperature physics.
contribution: He liquefied hydrogen and invented the vacuum flask, now commonly called a thermos, for thermal insulation.

name: Michael Faraday
bio: English scientist whose experiments established many of the foundations of modern electromagnetism.
contribution: His discoveries of electromagnetic induction, the laws of electrolysis, and diamagnetism shaped electric motors and generators.

name: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky
bio: Russian scientist and engineer who pioneered the theory of spaceflight and astronautics.
contribution: Developed the rocket equation and established theoretical foundations for multistage rockets and space exploration.

name: Isaac Newton
bio: English mathematician and physicist whose work helped establish classical mechanics.
contribution: Formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation and made foundational contributions to calculus and optics.

name: Stephen Hawking
bio: English theoretical physicist known for work on black holes and the origins of the universe.
contribution: Predicted that black holes emit radiation, now known as Hawking radiation.

name: Benjamin Franklin
bio: American printer, statesman, and natural philosopher who investigated electricity.
contribution: Experiments with electricity helped establish that lightning is electrical in nature; he also developed the lightning rod.

name: André-Marie Ampère
bio: French mathematician and physicist, regarded as one of the founders of electrodynamics.
contribution: Established mathematical foundations for electromagnetism; the ampere, the SI unit of electric current, is named in his honor.

name: Robert Boyle
bio: Anglo-Irish natural philosopher and chemist who helped shape experimental science.
contribution: Boyle's law describes the inverse relationship between the pressure and volume of a gas at constant temperature.

name: Rudolf Mössbauer
bio: German physicist whose research concerned the absorption of gamma rays by solids.
contribution: Discovered the recoil-free nuclear resonance absorption of gamma radiation, known as the Mössbauer effect.

name: Dmitri Mendeleev
bio: Russian chemist who organized the known chemical elements into a periodic system.
contribution: Created the periodic table and predicted the properties of elements that had not yet been discovered.

name: Thomas Edison
bio: American inventor whose work helped make electric lighting and sound recording practical.
contribution: Developed commercially practical electric-lighting systems and made major improvements to the phonograph.

name: Charles Darwin
bio: English naturalist whose observations transformed the study of life and its diversity.
contribution: Developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, presented in On the Origin of Species.

name: Galileo Galilei
bio: Italian astronomer and physicist whose observations and experiments advanced modern science.
contribution: Used telescopic observations to study the Moon, Jupiter's moons, and the phases of Venus, supporting a Sun-centered model.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus
bio: Renaissance astronomer who proposed a mathematical model with the Sun near the center of the planetary system.
contribution: His heliocentric model helped transform astronomy and the understanding of Earth's place in the cosmos.

name: Alexander Graham Bell
bio: Scottish-born inventor and teacher of the deaf who researched speech and sound transmission.
contribution: Patented an early practical telephone and continued research in communications and aeronautics.

name: Georg Ohm
bio: German physicist and mathematician who investigated electric circuits.
contribution: Established Ohm's law, relating voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical conductor.

name: René Descartes
bio: French philosopher, mathematician, and natural scientist whose work influenced modern mathematics and physics.
contribution: Developed analytic geometry, linking algebra and geometry through the Cartesian coordinate system.

name: William Harvey
bio: English physician who used observation and experiment to study the human body.
contribution: Demonstrated that the heart circulates blood through the body.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
bio: Italian artist, engineer, and investigator of anatomy, mechanics, and the natural world.
contribution: His notebooks recorded detailed observations and designs across anatomy, flight, engineering, and physics.

name: Max Planck
bio: German theoretical physicist whose work helped begin quantum theory.
contribution: Introduced the idea that energy is emitted in discrete quantities to explain black-body radiation.

name: Santiago Ramón y Cajal
bio: Spanish neuroscientist whose microscopic studies revealed the organization of the nervous system.
contribution: Established the neuron doctrine, showing that the nervous system is made of distinct cells.

name: Richard Feynman
bio: American theoretical physicist known for his work in quantum mechanics and engaging science teaching.
contribution: Developed a path-integral formulation of quantum mechanics and tools for calculations in quantum electrodynamics.

name: Williamina Fleming
bio: Scottish-American astronomer who helped develop systematic methods for classifying stars.
contribution: Catalogued stellar spectra and discovered the Horsehead Nebula while working at the Harvard Observatory.

name: Peter Higgs
bio: British theoretical physicist whose work concerned the origin of mass in particle physics.
contribution: Predicted a field associated with the Higgs boson, whose discovery confirmed a key part of the Standard Model.

name: Francis Crick
bio: British molecular biologist and physicist who helped uncover the structure of DNA.
contribution: With James Watson and colleagues, helped establish the double-helix structure of DNA and later studied the genetic code.

name: James Clerk Maxwell
bio: Scottish physicist whose theories unified electricity, magnetism, and light.
contribution: Formulated Maxwell's equations, which describe classical electromagnetism.

name: William Thomson, Lord Kelvin
bio: Mathematical physicist and engineer whose work shaped thermodynamics and electrical science.
contribution: Helped establish the absolute temperature scale, now called the kelvin scale.

name: George Everest
bio: Welsh surveyor and geographer who led the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India.
contribution: Advanced the precise surveying of the Indian subcontinent; Mount Everest was named in his honor.

name: Nikola Tesla
bio: Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer whose work advanced alternating-current power.
contribution: Developed key alternating-current motor and power-transmission technologies.

name: Robert Hooke
bio: English natural philosopher and experimenter who made contributions to physics, biology, and architecture.
contribution: Formulated Hooke's law of elasticity and used a microscope to describe cells in living material.

name: Gregor Mendel
bio: Moravian monk and scientist whose plant-breeding experiments helped establish genetics.
contribution: Identified basic patterns of inheritance through experiments with pea plants.

name: Ernst Mayr
bio: German-American evolutionary biologist and historian of science.
contribution: Helped shape the modern synthesis of evolutionary biology and clarified the biological species concept.

name: Alexander Fleming
bio: Scottish physician and microbiologist whose laboratory observations led to a major medical discovery.
contribution: Discovered penicillin, opening the way to modern antibiotic treatment.

name: Erwin Schrödinger
bio: Austrian theoretical physicist who made foundational contributions to quantum mechanics.
contribution: Developed the wave equation that bears his name and describes quantum states.

name: Antoine Lavoisier
bio: French chemist whose precise experiments helped establish modern chemistry.
contribution: Helped explain combustion through oxygen and formulated the law of conservation of mass in chemical reactions.

name: Max Delbrück
bio: German-American biophysicist who helped establish molecular biology as a research field.
contribution: Used bacteriophages to investigate gene replication and genetic structure.

name: Arthur Compton
bio: American physicist whose experiments studied the interaction of X-rays and matter.
contribution: Discovered the Compton effect, showing that X-rays behave as particles carrying momentum.

name: Niels Bohr
bio: Danish physicist who contributed to atomic theory and the development of quantum mechanics.
contribution: Proposed an influential model of the atom and helped develop the interpretation of quantum theory.

name: Enrico Fermi
bio: Italian-American physicist known for theoretical and experimental work in nuclear physics.
contribution: Developed the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction and made major contributions to quantum statistics.

name: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
bio: Indian-American astrophysicist whose work explained the structure and evolution of stars.
contribution: Identified the Chandrasekhar limit, the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf star.

name: James Chadwick
bio: English physicist whose experiments clarified the structure of the atomic nucleus.
contribution: Discovered the neutron, a fundamental component of atomic nuclei.

name: Alfred Nobel
bio: Swedish chemist, engineer, and inventor who held patents in several fields.
contribution: Invented dynamite and established the Nobel Prizes through his will.

name: Pierre-Gilles de Gennes
bio: French physicist whose research connected ideas in condensed matter physics with soft materials.
contribution: Advanced understanding of liquid crystals and polymers using concepts from phase transitions.

name: Carl Sagan
bio: American astronomer and science communicator who studied planets and the possibility of life beyond Earth.
contribution: Conducted influential planetary research and helped popularize astronomy for a broad audience.

name: William Herschel
bio: German-born British astronomer and telescope maker who surveyed the night sky.
contribution: Discovered Uranus and infrared radiation, and catalogued thousands of celestial objects.

name: Edwin Hubble
bio: American astronomer whose observations transformed the study of galaxies and the expanding universe.
contribution: Showed that galaxies exist beyond the Milky Way and found evidence that the universe is expanding.

name: Christian Doppler
bio: Austrian physicist and mathematician who studied the behavior of waves.
contribution: Described the Doppler effect, the change in observed frequency caused by relative motion.

name: Werner Heisenberg
bio: German theoretical physicist and a founder of quantum mechanics.
contribution: Formulated the uncertainty principle, which sets fundamental limits on simultaneous measurements of certain properties.

name: Max Born
bio: German-British theoretical physicist whose work shaped the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics.
contribution: Introduced the probability interpretation of the quantum wave function.

name: Henri Becquerel
bio: French physicist whose experiments revealed spontaneous radiation from uranium salts.
contribution: Discovered natural radioactivity, a finding that opened a new field of physics.

name: Charles Babbage
bio: English mathematician and inventor whose mechanical computing designs anticipated general-purpose computers.
contribution: Designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine, foundational concepts in the history of computing.

name: Benjamin Constant
bio: French-Swiss politician, writer on politics and religion (1767-2011)

name: Ivan Lapshin
bio: Russian philosopher, publicist, translator and teacher (1870–1952)

name: Marie Stopes
bio: British birth control campaigner and paleontologist (1880-1958)

name: Maria Teschler-Nicola
bio: researcher in the field of digital humanities

name: Geoffrey Vickers
bio: English military officer, lawyer, and systems scientist (1894–1982); recipient of the Victoria Cross

name: Kiyekbayev Zhalil G.
bio: Turkologist, Doctor of Philology, Bashkir writer (1911-1968)

name: A. Hari Reddi
bio: Professor of Musculoskeletal Molecular Biology at the University of California, Davis.

name: Don Cone
bio: Radio and internet technician and researcher, developed Packet Radio Van (1926–2011)

name: Virpi Hämeen-Anttila
bio: Finnish researcher, translator, illustrator and writer

name: Edward Strong
bio: Chancellor of the University of California at Berkeley between 1961 and 1965

name: Rudolf Zahradník
bio: Czech chemical engineer and chairman of the Czech Academy of Science

name: Vladimir Tikhomirov
bio: Soviet geologist and historian of science (1915-1994)

name: Andrzej Szmajke
bio: Polish professor of psychology, specializing in social and personality psychology, evolutionary psychology
